questions.q: A network with two hidden layers and a linear activation is trained on the spiral. What happens?
options: It learns the spiral, only slower
It can only draw a straight boundary, because linear layers stacked are one linear layer
It learns it faster than tanh
questions.answer: It can only draw a straight boundary, because linear layers stacked are one linear layer
questions.why: The lab shows two linear layers equal the single layer W2·W1 to 1e-16, and the linear network gets 45% of the held-out points right.

questions.q: With a sigmoid output and cross-entropy loss, what is the gradient of the loss at the output logit, for one point?
questions.why: The sigmoid's slope cancels against the loss's, which is why the lab's hand-written backward starts from p - y and matches autograd.

questions.q: A gradient check reports a relative error of 3e-9 for every weight. What does that tell you?
options: The backward pass computes the right derivatives
questions.answer: The backward pass computes the right derivatives
questions.why: It compares calculus with finite differences. It says nothing about whether training will succeed, which depends on the rate, the shape and the data.

questions.q: The training points are 100% right and the held-out rings are 70% right. What is going on?
options: The network memorised the training points more than it learned the shape
The learning rate is too small
Held-out points are always worse by 30%
questions.answer: The network memorised the training points more than it learned the shape
questions.why: Held-out points never move the weights, so they show how well the shape generalises. Try fewer neurons or less noise.
